findings.title: session.refresh() can be entered concurrently; the token swap is not atomic
findings.body_markdown: `refresh_session()` reads the refresh token, issues a new pair and deletes the old token in three statements (line 13). Two concurrent refreshes with one token could both succeed and leave two live sessions.

proof.test_code:
"""Repro for a prguard finding in app/auth/session.py::refresh_session.

Claim: two concurrent refreshes with one token both succeed.
"""

from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

from app.auth.session import refresh_session_outcome


def test_one_refresh_token_refreshes_once():
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=2) as pool:
        results = list(pool.map(refresh_session_outcome, ["rt_9f2c", "rt_9f2c"]))
    assert sorted(results) == ["ok", "reused"]

findings.title: revoke_session() deletes the access token but leaves its refresh token live
findings.body_markdown: With rotation on, `revoke_session()` removes the session's current access token (line 44) and not the refresh token issued with it, so a revoked session is back after one refresh.

"""Repro for a prguard finding in app/auth/session.py::revoke_session.

Claim: a revoked session can still be refreshed.
"""

from app.auth.session import refresh_after_revoke


def test_revoked_session_cannot_refresh():
    assert refresh_after_revoke("ses_77ab") is None
